classification.difficultyReason: The cumulative-frequency column scaffolds the first median. The second part requires removing the two oldest observations, updating the total and middle position, and locating the new median in the remaining distribution.

inlines.text: The table on the right shows the ages of students at an acting academy.
Fill in the cumulative frequency column to
The cumulative frequency is 7 through age 19 and 13 through age 20. The eighth observation is 20, so the median age is 20 years.
The two oldest students leave the academy.

answer.worked:
Both students aged $21$ leave.

$$\begin{align*}n&=15-2\\n&=13\\Mp&=\frac{13+1}{2}\\Mp&=7\end{align*}$$

The remaining cumulative frequencies are $2,7,13$ for ages $18,19,20$. The seventh observation has age $19$.

The new median age is $19$ years.
